Energetics, Inc. (2000). Energy and Environmental Profile of the U.S. Chemical Industry, Chapter 5: Agricultural Chemicals: Fertilizers. Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies, Washington DC, May 2000. pp.141-174.

Chapter 5 only (PDF of 34 pp., printed pp.141-174; no title page in the file, so publisher/date taken from the draft citation and PDF metadata title). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed - 140). Region: United States, 1997. Loaded: Tables 5-3 to 5-12 energy use per lb of product for ten processes - electricity (average and range), fuel for steam/process heat (derived as the sum of the four printed fuel rows) and NET PROCESS ENERGY as target total; energy export as an output steam flow (_flows); ammonia CO2-regenerator process CO2 (Table 5-13). Values are generic estimates built from licensor requirements, mostly reprinted (EFMA 1999, HP 1999, Enviro-Chem 1999, Brown 1996, PNNL 1994). Traps: (1) the split of fuel among oil/LPG, gas, coal and other is an allocation by the industry-wide 1997 fuel mix (77% gas, 10% coal, 10% other, 3% oil), so the individual fuel rows are in _other-values, not the main file; (2) ammonia natural gas includes feedstock; (3) Total Process Energy is primary (with electricity losses) and is not loaded; (4) Key Facts boxes print net-of-export figures (urea 732, ammonium phosphate 206, nitric acid net steam 311) that differ from the tables; (5) text says wet phosphoric acid needs about 6,130 Btu/lb versus 1,810 net in Table 5-9 and the furnace process share is 4% in tables vs 10% in text. Heating-value basis not stated (U.S. practice is HHV). Air emission tables other than ammonia CO2 are non-GHG and skipped; effluent standards skipped.
